items.justification: Per-device uniqueness of security parameters versus ongoing infrastructure risk review; no shared objective.
Hardware memory access control versus documentation content for training data.
Both restrict privileged access to system interfaces; A gates configuration behind authentication, B limits inter-system permissions to what functionality requires.
Vetted cryptographic implementations versus supporting operators through model version changes.
Cryptographic agility versus usage guidance on model limitations.
Both target controlled evolution of software assets; A requires updateability, B requires version control and asset tracking.
Brute-force resistance versus risk from superfluous model capability.
Shared access-control objective; A mandates a credential-change mechanism on the device, B mandates evaluation of organizational access-control frameworks.
Cryptographic protection in transit versus secure disposal on ownership transfer.
Network input validation versus audit-trail documentation.
Both concern secure development practice; A names process and toolchain hardening, B names environment separation and least privilege.
Update timeliness and asset version tracking are distinct objectives that together sustain secure software maintenance.
Update authenticity verification versus incident management and recovery planning.
Recorded justifications for non-applicable provisions and contractual flow-down to cloud providers are different routes to the same assurance posture.
User notification of disruptive updates versus use of independent security testers.
Both bear on secure configuration but from opposite ends: user-facing verification guidance versus internal threat modelling when configuration changes.
Input validation versus disaster recovery planning.
Continued assurance of a secure state, approached through user self-checks and through operator-side behavioural monitoring.
A requires informing the user that an update is needed; B covers producing the update, notifying operators, and delivering it to end-users, which includes A's notification duty.
Vetted cryptographic implementations versus assurance over external risk owners.
User data erasure versus pre-build requirements and risk assessment.
Both protect security-critical assets; A over the lifecycle of critical security parameters, B through access-control measures on APIs, models and data.
Vulnerability disclosure policy versus data and input sanitisation.
Secure boot verification versus usage guidance.
User control over automatic updates versus separated development environments.
Resilience to network and power loss versus confidentiality of sensitive data.
Authentication before configuration change versus monitoring internal model states.
Disclosure policy publication versus confidentiality of model weights.
Cryptography securing the update channel versus confidentiality protection for training data and weights; both invoke protection but pursue different objectives.
Authenticated configuration change versus asset disposal at handover.
Input validation versus patch provision and delivery.
A is a specific update-integrity control, B the threat-modelling process that would identify the need for such controls; distinct objectives, jointly effective.
Key lifecycle management versus disaster recovery planning.
Both mandate validation and sanitisation of untrusted input; A at the device user interface, B across model data and inputs.
Both require verification that security functionality is correctly implemented, A through reviewed implementations and B through checking specified controls were built in.
Installation usability versus behavioural performance monitoring.
Per-device parameter uniqueness versus due diligence on external components.
Both concern dissemination of security update information, but to different audiences: end-user notification control versus internal staff awareness channels.
Setup guidance for users versus asset tracking and version control.
Disruption notification versus development environment separation.
